subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of an affine plane spanned by an orthonormal frame is the image of Lebesgue measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let w = (w_0, …, w_{m−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (= Euclid P), a ∈ ℝ^P, and S := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y − a ∈ span(w_0, …, w_{m−1})}, the affine m-plane through a spanned by w. Let ℝ^m := Fin m → ℝ carry the product Lebesgue measure Lᵐ (volume) and j : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, j(z) := a + Σ_i z_i w_i. Then (i) the image measure j_*(Lᵐ) equals Hᵐ⌞S, where Hᵐ = μHE[m]; (ii) S is closed; (iii) (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (iv) (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) > 0 for every r > 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (w : Fin m → Euclid P) (a : Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ w → Measure.map (fun z : Fin m → ℝ => a + ∑ i, z i • w i) volume = (μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ IsClosed {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) K < ∞) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) (ball a r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_j z_j v_j, a linear isometry onto V₀; Hⁿ⌞V₀ = ι_*(Lⁿ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume)"), stated for an arbitrary affine plane and with the local finiteness and positivity used in steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 of that proof. Write Euclid m := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Euclidean norm) and toLp : (Fin m → ℝ) → Euclid m for the identity on coordinates (WithLp.toLp 2).

1. (Isometric parametrisation.) Define J : Euclid m → ℝ^P, J(u) := a + Σ_i u_i w_i. For c ∈ Euclid m, orthonormality gives ⟨Σ_i c_i w_i, Σ_i c_i w_i⟩ = Σ_i c_i² (Orthonormal.inner_sum), and Σ_i c_i² = ‖c‖² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq); since both norms are ≥ 0, ‖Σ_i c_i w_i‖ = ‖c‖. Hence ‖J(u) − J(u′)‖ = ‖Σ_i (u_i − u′_i) w_i‖ = ‖u − u′‖, i.e. J is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq).

2. (Range.) range(J) = S. Indeed y = J(u) iff y − a = Σ_i u_i w_i; conversely, if y − a ∈ span(w) then y − a = Σ_i c_i w_i for some c : Fin m → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, Fin m being finite), and y = J(toLp c).

3. (Hausdorff measure under the isometry.) For an isometry, the image of μHE[m] is μHE[m] restricted to the range (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), and μHE[m] on Euclid m is the Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By step 2, J_*(L_Euclid) = Hᵐ⌞S, where L_Euclid is the Lebesgue measure (volume) of Euclid m.

4. (Proof of (i).) j = J ∘ toLp, and toLp is measure preserving from the product Lebesgue measure of Fin m → ℝ to the Lebesgue measure of Euclid m (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). Both maps are continuous, hence measurable, so j_*(Lᵐ) = J_*(toLp_*(Lᵐ)) = J_*(L_Euclid) = Hᵐ⌞S (Measure.map_map and step 3).

5. (Proof of (ii).) S is the preimage of the linear subspace span(w) under the continuous map y ↦ y − a; span(w) is finite-dimensional, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). So S is closed (and in particular Borel).

6. (Proof of (iii).) Let K be compact; K is closed, hence Borel, so by step 3 (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) = J_*(L_Euclid)(K) = L_Euclid(J⁻¹(K)) (Measure.map_apply). An isometry defined on a complete space is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), so J⁻¹(K) is compact (IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage), and compact sets have finite Lebesgue measure. Hence (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) < ∞.

7. (Proof of (iv).) Let r > 0. As in step 6, (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) = L_Euclid(J⁻¹(B_r(a))). The set J⁻¹(B_r(a)) is open (J is continuous) and contains 0 because J(0) = a. Nonempty open sets have positive Lebesgue measure (IsOpen.measure_pos; L_Euclid is an additive Haar measure, also for m = 0, where Euclid 0 is a single point of measure 1). Hence (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: J(u) = a + Σ_i u_i w_i is an isometry of Euclid m onto S (orthonormality: ‖Σ c_i w_i‖ = ‖c‖; range by mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
J_*(Lebesgue) = μHE[m]⌞S by Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; composing with the measure-preserving toLp gives (i).
S is the preimage of a finite-dimensional (closed) subspace, so closed.
(Hᵐ⌞S)(K) = Leb(J⁻¹K) < ∞ since J is a closed embedding; (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) = Leb(J⁻¹B_r(a)) > 0 since this open set contains 0.

subproblems.title: Integrals of partial derivatives of a compactly supported C¹ function over a coordinate half-space
subproblems.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, let ℝ^{d+1} := Fin (d+1) → ℝ and ℝ^d := Fin d → ℝ carry the product Lebesgue measures (volume), let g : ℝ^{d+1} → ℝ be C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1) with compact support, t ∈ ℝ, and H := {z ∈ ℝ^{d+1} : z_0 < t}. Write ∂_i g(z) := Dg(z)(e_i) with e_i = Pi.single i 1, and (t, z′) := Fin.cons t z′ for z′ ∈ ℝ^d. Then (a) ∫_H ∂_i g(z) dz = 0 for every i ≠ 0, and (b) ∫_H ∂_0 g(z) dz = ∫_{ℝ^d} g(t, z′) dz′.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (g : (Fin (d + 1) → ℝ) → ℝ) (t : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), i ≠ 0 → ∫ z in {z : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ | z 0 < t}, fderiv ℝ g z (Pi.single i 1) = 0) ∧ ∫ z in {z : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ | z 0 < t}, fderiv ℝ g z (Pi.single 0 1) = ∫ z' : Fin d → ℝ, g (Fin.cons t z')
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("For j ≥ 2, integrating first in z_j over ℝ gives 0; for j = 1, ∫_{z_1<t}∂_1φ̃_1dz = ∫_{ℝ^{n−1}}φ̃_1(t, z′)dz′"; the coordinates are indexed from 0 here), i.e. Fubini's theorem and the fundamental theorem of calculus, written for one C¹ function with compact support. Norms on ℝ^{d+1} are sup norms (only used for boundedness).

1. (Support bound.) tsupport g is compact, hence bounded: tsupport g ⊆ B̄_R(0) for some R ∈ ℝ. If ‖z‖ > R then z ∉ tsupport g, so g(z) = 0; and since tsupport(Dg) ⊆ tsupport g (tsupport_fderiv_subset), also Dg(z) = 0.

2. (Coordinate lines.) For i ∈ Fin (d+1) and y ∈ ℝ^d let ℓ(s) := insertNth i s y ∈ ℝ^{d+1} (i-th coordinate s, coordinate i.succAbove k equal to y_k). Checking coordinates, ℓ(s) = ℓ(0) + s·e_i, so ℓ is affine with derivative e_i, and |s| = |ℓ(s)_i| ≤ ‖ℓ(s)‖. By the chain rule h(s) := g(ℓ(s)) is differentiable with h′(s) = Dg(ℓ(s))(e_i) = ∂_i g(ℓ(s)) for every s ∈ ℝ.

3. (Behaviour of h.) If |s| > |R| then ‖ℓ(s)‖ > R, so h(s) = 0 and h′(s) = 0 by step 1. Hence h → 0 at −∞ and at +∞ (it is eventually 0), and h′ is continuous (g is C¹) with support in [−|R|, |R|], hence integrable on ℝ.

4. (Fubini.) The map z ↦ (z_i, removeNth i z) is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence ℝ^{d+1} → ℝ × ℝ^d (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove, volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove) whose inverse is (s, y) ↦ insertNth i s y. The function G := 1_H·∂_i g is integrable on ℝ^{d+1}: ∂_i g is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply) and H is Borel. Hence G ∘ (inverse) is integrable for the product measure (MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb), and by change of variables and Fubini (MeasurePreserving.integral_comp′, integral_prod_symm):
   ∫_H ∂_i g = ∫ G = ∫_{y∈ℝ^d} ( ∫_{s∈ℝ} G(insertNth i s y) ds ) dy.

5. (Proof of (a).) Let i ≠ 0. Then d ≥ 1 (Fin 1 has only the element 0), and 0 = i.succAbove 0 (Fin.succAbove_ne_zero_zero), so (insertNth i s y)_0 = y_0 does not depend on s. For fixed y the inner integral is therefore 0 if y_0 ≥ t, and equals ∫_ℝ h′(s) ds if y_0 < t, where h is the function of step 2 for this i and y. By steps 2–3 and the fundamental theorem of calculus on ℝ (integral_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto), ∫_ℝ h′ = 0 − 0 = 0. Thus every inner integral vanishes and ∫_H ∂_i g = 0.

6. (Proof of (b).) Let i = 0. Then insertNth 0 s y = Fin.cons s y (Fin.insertNth_zero′) has 0-th coordinate s, so for fixed y the inner integral is ∫_{s<t} h′(s) ds = ∫_{(−∞, t)} h′ = ∫_{(−∞, t]} h′ (a point is Lebesgue-null; integral_Iic_eq_integral_Iio). By steps 2–3 and the fundamental theorem of calculus on a half-line (integral_Iic_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto′), this equals h(t) − lim_{s→−∞} h(s) = g(Fin.cons t y) − 0. Integrating over y ∈ ℝ^d gives ∫_H ∂_0 g = ∫_{ℝ^d} g(t, y) dy. ∎
proof_key_steps: g and Dg vanish outside a ball B̄_R(0); along the line s ↦ insertNth i s y, h(s) = g(…) has h′ = ∂_i g(…), vanishes for |s| > |R|, and h′ is integrable.
Fubini through the measure-preserving equivalence z ↦ (z_i, removeNth i z): ∫_H ∂_i g = ∫_y ∫_s 1_H ∂_i g(insertNth i s y) ds dy.
i ≠ 0: membership in H does not depend on s, and ∫_ℝ h′ = 0 by the fundamental theorem of calculus.
i = 0: the inner integral is ∫_{(−∞,t]} h′ = h(t) = g(Fin.cons t y).

Uses the siblings plane_measure (P1) and halfspace_ftc (P2). ℝ^k := Fin k → ℝ with product Lebesgue measure; e_i := Pi.single i 1.

1. (Parametrisation of V₀.) Let ι : ℝ^{d+1} → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_i z_i v_i, a continuous linear map with ι(e_i) = v_i. By orthonormality ⟨v_i, ι(z)⟩ = z_i (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype); in particular ⟨ι(z), v_0⟩ = z_0 and ι is injective, hence a closed embedding (LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective; the domain is finite-dimensional). By (P1)(i) with m := d+1, w := v, a := 0 (note {y : y − 0 ∈ V₀} = V₀ and 0 + Σ_i z_i v_i = ι(z)): ι_*(L^{d+1}) = Hⁿ⌞V₀.

2. (The integrand in coordinates.) Let F(y) := dφ(y)(v). Since φ is smooth with compact support, so is dφ (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm), and F is continuous. For i ∈ Fin (d+1) let G_i(y) := φ(y)(removeNth i v) (smooth, compact support inside tsupport φ) and g_i := G_i ∘ ι, which is C¹ with compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding). By the chain rule, ∂_i g_i(z) := Dg_i(z)(e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(ι e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(v_i). The coordinate formula of the exterior derivative (exteriorDerivative_apply: dω(x)(u) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[ω(·)(removeNth i u)](x)(u_i)) gives, for every z,
   F(ι z) = Σ_i (−1)^i ∂_i g_i(z).

3. (Left side of (b) in coordinates.) H_t := {y : ⟨y, v_0⟩ < t} is open, hence Borel. Restricting first to V₀ and then to H_t (Measure.restrict_restrict) and using step 1 and the change of variables for image measures (setIntegral_map; F is continuous, ι measurable):
   ∫_{V₀∩H_t} F dHⁿ = ∫_{H_t} F d(ι_*L^{d+1}) = ∫_{ι⁻¹(H_t)} F(ι z) dz = ∫_{{z : z_0 < t}} F(ι z) dz,
   since ι⁻¹(H_t) = {z : z_0 < t} by step 1. Each function z ↦ (−1)^i ∂_i g_i(z) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable on {z_0 < t}, so by step 2 and linearity (integral_finset_sum, integral_const_mul) the left side equals Σ_i (−1)^i ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_i g_i(z) dz.

4. (Apply (P2).) For i ≠ 0 (i.e. i = k+1, k ∈ Fin d), (P2)(a) applied to g_i gives ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_i g_i = 0. For i = 0, (P2)(b) applied to g_0 gives ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_0 g_0 = ∫_{ℝ^d} g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′. Splitting off the index 0 (Fin.sum_univ_succ), the left side of (b) equals ∫_{ℝ^d} g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′.

5. (Right side of (b) in coordinates.) Fin.tail v = (v_1, …, v_d) is orthonormal (a subfamily of v: Orthonormal.comp with the injective Fin.succ). By (P1)(i) with m := d, w := Fin.tail v, a := t v_0: j_*(L^d) = H^d⌞L_t, where j(z′) := t v_0 + Σ_k z′_k v_{k+1}. As y ↦ φ(y)(Fin.tail v) is continuous, ∫_{L_t} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y) = ∫_{ℝ^d} φ(j(z′))(Fin.tail v) dz′ (integral_map).

6. (Identification; proof of (b).) removeNth 0 v = Fin.tail v (Fin.removeNth_zero), and ι(Fin.cons t z′) = t v_0 + Σ_k z′_k v_{k+1} = j(z′) (Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ). Hence g_0(Fin.cons t z′) = φ(j(z′))(Fin.tail v) for every z′, and steps 4 and 5 give (b).

7. (Proof of (a).) tsupport φ is compact, so there is C with |⟨y, v_0⟩| ≤ C on tsupport φ (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn); put T := C + 1, so ⟨y, v_0⟩ < T for y ∈ tsupport φ. Since tsupport(dφ) ⊆ tsupport φ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), F vanishes on V₀ \ (V₀ ∩ H_T); V₀ is closed (finite-dimensional subspace), hence Borel, so ∫_{V₀} F dHⁿ = ∫_{V₀∩H_T} F dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero), which by (b) equals ∫_{L_T} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y). For y ∈ L_T write y − T v_0 = Σ_k c_k v_{k+1} (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun); orthonormality gives ⟨y − T v_0, v_0⟩ = 0, so ⟨y, v_0⟩ = T‖v_0‖² = T. Thus y ∉ tsupport φ, φ(y) = 0 and the integrand vanishes on L_T. Therefore ∫_{V₀} dφ(y)(v) dHⁿ(y) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(z) = Σ z_i v_i is a closed linear embedding with ⟨ι z, v_0⟩ = z_0 and ι_*(Leb) = Hⁿ⌞V₀ (plane_measure).
dφ(ι z)(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i ∂_i g_i(z) with g_i = φ(ι ·)(removeNth i v) (exteriorDerivative_apply, chain rule).
∫_{V₀∩{⟨y,v_0⟩<t}} dφ(v) dHⁿ = Σ_i (−1)^i ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_i g_i = ∫ g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′ (halfspace_ftc).
∫_{L_t} φ(Fin.tail v) dH^d = ∫ φ(t v_0 + Σ z′_k v_{k+1})(Fin.tail v) dz′ (plane_measure), which is the same integral since removeNth 0 v = Fin.tail v.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity weight equal to c times Hausdorff measure on a set forces c to be a natural number
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple (IMRep U m) with weight R.measure = (Hᵐ⌞M) withDensity θ (Hᵐ = μHE[m], θ : ℝ^P → ℕ), S ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set and c > 0 a real number. Assume (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) < ∞ for every compact K, (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(x)) > 0 for some x ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ, and R.measure(G) = c·(Hᵐ⌞S)(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (c read as ENNReal.ofReal c). Then c is a natural number: c = k for some k ∈ ℕ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U m) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → MeasurableSet S → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict S) K < ∞) → (∃ (x : Euclid P) (r : ℝ), 0 < ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict S) (ball x r)) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → R.measure G = ENNReal.ofReal c * ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict S) G) → ∃ k : ℕ, c = k
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 6 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("the Borel measures R.measure and θ₀H^d⌞L_t agree on all open sets … so R.measure = θ₀H^d⌞L_t (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion)"; "θ′ = θ₀ H^d-a.e. on D ∩ M_t (ae_eq_of_forall_setLIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite) … θ′ takes values in ℕ, so θ₀ = θ′(x) ∈ ℕ"), for a general Borel set S in place of the plane L_t and a general ball in place of B_1(tv_1). Write ν := Hᵐ⌞S, M := R.carrier (Borel), θ := R.mult (measurable, ℕ-valued).

1. (Finiteness on balls.) For every ball, ν(B_ρ(z)) ≤ ν(B̄_ρ(z)) < ∞, because closed balls of ℝ^P are compact.

2. (R.measure = c·ν.) The open subsets of ℝ^P form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) generating the Borel σ-algebra (BorelSpace.measurable_eq). The open balls B_{j+1}(0), j ∈ ℕ, cover ℝ^P (iUnion_ball_nat_succ) and R.measure(B_{j+1}(0)) = c·ν(B_{j+1}(0)) < ∞ by the hypothesis and step 1. By hypothesis R.measure and c·ν agree on every open set, so by the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on a generating π-system with a finite cover (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion), R.measure = c·ν.

3. (A set of positive finite measure.) Let x, r be as in the hypothesis and D := S ∩ B_r(x), a Borel set. Then Hᵐ(D) = ν(B_r(x)) (Measure.restrict_apply), so 0 < Hᵐ(D) < ∞ by the hypothesis and step 1.

4. (Formula for the weight.) For Borel E, R.measure(E) = ∫_E θ d(Hᵐ⌞M) = ∫_{E∩M} θ dHᵐ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict).

5. (D is essentially inside M.) By step 4, R.measure(D \ M) = ∫_{(D\M)∩M} θ dHᵐ = 0, since (D \ M) ∩ M = ∅. By step 2 and D \ M ⊆ S, R.measure(D \ M) = c·Hᵐ((D \ M) ∩ S) = c·Hᵐ(D \ M). As c > 0 (so ENNReal.ofReal c ≠ 0), Hᵐ(D \ M) = 0, and therefore Hᵐ(D ∩ M) = Hᵐ(D) > 0 (measure_inter_add_diff).

6. (θ = c almost everywhere on D ∩ M.) Let μ′ := Hᵐ⌞(D ∩ M), a finite measure since μ′(ℝ^P) = Hᵐ(D ∩ M) = Hᵐ(D) < ∞. For every Borel E, using steps 4 and 2, D ⊆ S, and Hᵐ((E ∩ D) \ M) ≤ Hᵐ(D \ M) = 0:
   ∫_E θ dμ′ = ∫_{E∩D∩M} θ dHᵐ = R.measure(E ∩ D) = c·Hᵐ(E ∩ D ∩ S) = c·Hᵐ(E ∩ D) = c·Hᵐ(E ∩ D ∩ M) = ∫_E c dμ′.
   The functions x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) and the constant c are measurable and μ′ is σ-finite, so θ = c μ′-almost everywhere (ae_eq_of_forall_setLIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite).

7. (Conclusion.) μ′ ≠ 0 because μ′(ℝ^P) = Hᵐ(D ∩ M) > 0 (step 5), so the almost-everywhere filter of μ′ is non-trivial (ae_neBot) and there is a point y with (θ(y) : [0, ∞]) = ENNReal.ofReal c. Taking real parts (c ≥ 0, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal) gives c = θ(y) with θ(y) ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.measure and c·Hᵐ⌞S agree on the π-system of open sets and are finite on the balls B_{j+1}(0), so they are equal.
For D = S ∩ B_r(x): 0 < Hᵐ(D) < ∞ and R.measure(D \ M) = 0 forces Hᵐ(D \ M) = 0, so Hᵐ(D ∩ M) > 0.
Set-lintegrals of θ and of the constant c agree on every Borel set for the finite measure Hᵐ⌞(D ∩ M), so θ = c a.e. there.
A point of the non-null set where θ = c gives c = θ(y) ∈ ℕ.

subproblems.title: Almost every half-space slice of a positive multiple of an oriented plane with the integer slice property is an integer multiplicity multiple of the boundary plane
subproblems.statement: (SL) is the exact frozen statement of the DAG theorem cmc_slice_mass_bounds (a hypothesis of the selected parent cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat, copied verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement): for P, k ∈ ℕ, an open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), Borel measures μ, μ′ finite on compact subsets of U, fields ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}, ξ′ : ℝ^P → Λ_k that are μ- resp. μ′-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and |ξ′(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ′-a.e., T(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) and ∂T(η) = ∫ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′(x) for all test forms, and an L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x), B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′(x), ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W. Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P, Hᵐ = μHE[m] (Mathlib's normalised Euclidean Hausdorff measure; μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure), |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for a covector α, Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors), a test k-form is an element of TestFormOn univ k, dφ = exteriorDerivative φ, ∂T(η) = T(dη). An admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) is a Borel measure μ finite on compact sets with a μ-a.e. strongly measurable ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., and X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. Then for L¹-almost every t ∈ ℝ there is an integer multiplicity current Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with Z(φ) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(v_1, …, v_d)dH^d(y) for every test d-form φ, where L_t := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y − t v_0 ∈ span(v_1, …, v_d)} and (v_1, …, v_d) = Fin.tail v.

Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("(μ, ξ) := (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, ξ_v) … is an admissible representation of C … (0, 0) represents ∂C = 0. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, this data, f, L := 1 … ISP of C … gives an L¹-null set N such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity for every t ∉ N"), together with step 1 (∂C = 0) and the formula of step 3, both supplied by the sibling plane_stokes (PS). Also uses the siblings plane_measure (PM) and covector_eval_le (O1).

1. (Representation of C.) Let μ := θ₀·(Hⁿ⌞V₀) (the scalar ENNReal.ofReal θ₀; θ₀ > 0), ξ_v ∈ Λ_n the evaluation at v, ξ_v(α) := α(v_0, …, v_d) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v), and ξ(x) := ξ_v for all x.
   (a) μ is finite on compact sets: by (PM)(iii) with m := n, w := v, a := 0 (where {y : y − 0 ∈ V₀} = V₀), Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ K) < ∞, hence μ(K) = θ₀Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ K) < ∞.
   (b) ξ is constant, hence a.e. strongly measurable, and |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(v)| ≤ |α| for every α by (O1) (v is orthonormal).
   (c) For every test n-form ω, ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) = (ENNReal.ofReal θ₀).toReal·∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = C(ω) (integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal).

2. (∂C = 0 and its representation.) For a test d-form η, ∂C(η) = C(dη) = θ₀∫_{V₀}dη(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀·0 = 0 by (PS)(a). Take μ′ := 0 and ξ′ := 0: μ′ is finite, ξ′ is constant, the bound holds trivially (μ′-a.e. statements are vacuous for μ′ = 0), and ∫ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′ = 0 = ∂C(η).

3. (The slicing function.) f(y) := ⟨y, v_0⟩ is 1-Lipschitz: |f(y) − f(y′)| = |⟨y − y′, v_0⟩| ≤ ‖y − y′‖·‖v_0‖ = ‖y − y′‖ (Cauchy–Schwarz, ‖v_0‖ = 1).

4. (Slices from (SL).) Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P (open), k := d, T := C, the data (μ, ξ), (μ′, ξ′) of steps 1–2 (finiteness on compact subsets of U by step 1(a)), f of step 3 and L := 1. This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′(x) for all t and test forms; only these two formulas are used.

5. (Integer multiplicity from ISP.) The hypotheses of ISP for (μ, ξ), (μ′, ξ′), f, L = 1 are exactly steps 1–3. Hence there is an L¹-null set N such that for t ∉ N every pair (A, B) with the two integral formulas has ∂A − B integer multiplicity. For t ∉ N the pair (A_t, B_t) of step 4 qualifies, so Z := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity. (Lean: filter_upwards on the ∀ᵐ t given by ISP.)

6. (Formula for Z.) Fix t ∉ N and a test d-form φ. By the contract's subtraction of currents and ∂A(φ) = A(dφ), Z(φ) = A_t(dφ) − B_t(φ). Here B_t(φ) = ∫ … d(μ′⌞{f<t}) = 0 since μ′ = 0 (Measure.restrict_zero, integral_zero_measure). The half-space {f < t} is open, hence Borel, so μ⌞{f<t} = θ₀·Hⁿ⌞({f<t} ∩ V₀) (Measure.restrict_smul, Measure.restrict_restrict) and
   A_t(dφ) = θ₀∫_{V₀∩{⟨y,v_0⟩<t}} dφ(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(v_1, …, v_d)dH^d(y)
   by (PS)(b). Hence Z(φ) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(Fin.tail v)dH^d(y) for every test d-form φ, for every t ∉ N, i.e. for L¹-a.e. t. ∎
proof_key_steps: (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, constant evaluation at v) is an admissible representation of C: local finiteness by plane_measure, bound by covector_eval_le, formula by integral_smul_measure.

subproblems.title: Evaluation on an orthonormal frame is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, α an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact (O) and consequence (O1) of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²)"). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_eval_le-a1, status accepted, candidate b7846b6), reused at its byte-identical frozen type; its formalization follows exactly this argument (via its accepted children regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basis_invariant, regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basisFun, regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis). Write Q(f) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² for an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P, and e for the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).

1. (Q does not depend on the orthonormal basis.) Let b, b′ be orthonormal bases and c(i, s) := ⟨b′_s, b_i⟩, so b_i = Σ_s c(i, s) b′_s. Multilinearity gives α(b∘j) = Σ_{a : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_k c(j(k), a(k))) α(b′∘a). Squaring and summing over j, the j-sum factors over the slots: Σ_j Π_k c(j(k), a(k)) c(j(k), a′(k)) = Π_k Σ_i c(i, a(k)) c(i, a′(k)), and Σ_i c(i, s) c(i, s′) = ⟨b′_s, b′_{s′}⟩ = δ_{ss′} (Parseval for b, orthonormality of b′). Hence all cross terms with a ≠ a′ vanish and Q(b) = Σ_a α(b′∘a)² = Q(b′).

2. (Q(e) = n!|α|².) Terms with non-injective j vanish (an alternating form vanishes on a tuple with two equal entries). Every injective j is uniquely I∘σ with I strictly increasing and σ a permutation of Fin n (I enumerates range(j) increasingly), and α(e∘(I∘σ)) = sgn(σ)α(e∘I), whose square is α(e∘I)². So Q(e) = Σ_{I increasing} n!·α(e∘I)² = n!|α|² by the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm.

3. (Extension of τ.) Orthonormal vectors are linearly independent, so n ≤ P, and τ extends to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f(ι(k)) = τ_k for k ∈ Fin n, where ι := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) is injective.

4. (Comparison.) For each permutation π of Fin n, j := ι∘π is injective, the maps π ↦ ι∘π are pairwise distinct, and α(f∘(ι∘π)) = α(τ∘π) = sgn(π)α(τ), whose square is α(τ)². All other terms of Q(f) are squares, hence ≥ 0. Therefore n!·α(τ)² ≤ Q(f) = Q(e) = n!|α|² (steps 1–2), so α(τ)² ≤ |α|² and |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (both sides ≥ 0). For n = 0 the family τ is empty, the only j is the empty map and the statement reads |α(())| ≤ |α(())|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Σ_j α(f∘j)² is independent of the orthonormal basis f (multilinear expansion and Parseval).
For the standard basis it equals n!|α|² (alternation and the increasing-index/permutation decomposition).
Extending τ to an orthonormal basis, the n! permuted copies of τ contribute n!α(τ)² ≤ n!|α|².

subproblems.title: A unit covector norming an orthonormal frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then there is an n-covector β on ℝ^P with |β| = covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 and β(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 ∧ β τ = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: consequence (O2) of Fact (O) in the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat ("β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k))"). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_norming-a1, status accepted, candidate baaca6e), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. We use the identity Q(f) = n!|β|² for every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P, where Q(f) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} β(f∘j)² (steps 1–2 of the proof of the sibling covector_eval_le, which apply to every n-covector).

1. (Definition.) For u = (u_0, …, u_{n−1}) let β(u) := det(⟨u_i, τ_l⟩)_{i,l ∈ Fin n}. The matrix entries are linear in u_i (row i), and the determinant is multilinear and alternating in its rows, so β is multilinear and alternating; on the finite-dimensional space (ℝ^P)^n it is continuous. Hence β is an n-covector.

2. (β(τ) = 1.) ⟨τ_i, τ_l⟩ = δ_{il} by orthonormality, so β(τ) = det(I_n) = 1.

3. (Values on a basis extending τ.) As in step 3 of covector_eval_le, extend τ to an orthonormal basis f with f(ι(k)) = τ_k, ι := Fin.castLE injective. For j : Fin n → Fin P the matrix of β(f∘j) has entries ⟨f_{j(i)}, τ_l⟩ = ⟨f_{j(i)}, f_{ι(l)}⟩ = δ_{j(i), ι(l)}. If some j(i) ∉ range(ι), row i is zero and β(f∘j) = 0. If j is not injective, two rows coincide and β(f∘j) = 0. Otherwise j = ι∘π for a permutation π of Fin n, the matrix is a permutation matrix and β(f∘j) = ±1.

4. (|β| = 1.) By step 3, Q(f) = Σ_π 1 = n!, so n!|β|² = Q(f) = n!, |β|² = 1 and |β| = 1 since |β| ≥ 0. For n = 0, β is the constant covector 1 (determinant of the empty matrix), β(()) = 1 and |β| = |β(())| = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: β(u) := det(⟨u_i, τ_l⟩) is a continuous alternating n-linear form with β(τ) = det I = 1.
On an orthonormal basis extending τ, β(f∘j) is ±1 exactly for j = ι∘π and 0 otherwise.
Hence n!|β|² = Σ_j β(f∘j)² = n!, so |β| = 1.
